headline: Marcos Administration Backs Proposed EO to Streamline Water-Sector Permits
deck: The Marcos administration is pursuing a proposed executive order intended to improve coordination and streamline permitting in the water sector.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Marcos administration is pushing a proposed executive order intended to strengthen water governance by streamlining permitting and public-service delivery, according to the Philippine Information Agency.

Anti-Red Tape Authority Secretary Ernesto Perez said the proposal was targeted for presidential approval before the end of October. The executive order had not yet been signed when the statement was made.

sections.heading: What we know
paragraphs: Perez said the proposed order would establish an Anti-Red Tape Advisory Council to improve regulatory coordination and ease of doing business in the water sector.

Under the proposal described at the Water Forum 2026 in Quezon City, the council would be chaired by the secretary of trade and industry and co-chaired by the ARTA director general. Representatives from finance, local government, information and communications technology, and the private sector would participate.

sections.heading: Background
paragraphs: Water projects often require coordination among several national and local authorities. The proposed reform is intended to reduce bureaucratic delays while improving coordination and access to government services.

sections.heading: What remains unclear
paragraphs: The final text, exact processing deadlines, agency responsibilities and implementing rules will remain uncertain until the executive order is approved and published.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: Water-sector permitting affects the pace of projects related to supply, sanitation and other essential services. Faster processing could help projects move forward, but clear safeguards and transparent rules remain necessary.

sections.heading: What happens next
paragraphs: The proposal may be refined before it is submitted for presidential approval. If signed, the government would still need to publish the order and explain how the new coordination mechanism will operate.
